Prerequisites: While there are no formal prerequisites, strong mathematical skills and a basic understanding of microeconomic theory would be helpful. Textbook: None is required but having one of 1 or 2 in the following is highly recommended. For auction theory, 6 is the standard reference. 1 Tadelis, Steven. Game theory: an introduction. Princeton university press, 2013. 2 Gibbons, Robert S.Game theory for applied economists.Princeton University Press, 1992. 3 Osborne, Martin J., and Ariel Rubinstein.A course in game theory. MIT press, 1994. 4 Osborne, Martin J.An introduction to game theory.Oxford university press, 2004. 5 Binmore, Ken.Playing for real: a text on game theory. Oxford university press, 2007. 6 Krishna, Vijay.Auction theory.Academic press, 2009. 3

Tentative Course Schedule Week 1 Introduction to game theory Week 2 Static games of complete information (Normal-form game) Week 3 Static games of complete information Week 4 Dynamic games of complete information (Extensive-form game) Week 5 Dynamic games of complete information (Subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium) Week 6 Static games of incomplete information (Bayesian Nash equilibrium) Week 7 Auction theory Week 8 Midterm Exam 4

Tentative Course Schedule (continued) Week 9 Mechanism design (Optimal mechanism) Week 10 Market Design (Matching theory) Week 11 Dynamic games of incomplete information (Perfect Bayesian equilibrium) Week 12 Dynamic games of incomplete information (Signaling game) Week 13 Cooperative game theory (Core and Shapley Value) Week 14 Bargaining Week 15 Additional topics and Review Week 16 Final Group Presentation This schedule is subject to change if necessary. 5
